summary: Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists countries whose citizens can enter without a visa under standing arrangements, among them the US (up to 90 days), Germany, Canada and Japan (up to 30 days), South Korea (up to 90 days, until 31 December 2026, for tourism only), Kazakhstan, Brazil and the UAE. Mongolia's Immigration Agency says the Government has exempted nationals of 34 countries, among them France, Spain, Italy, the UK, Australia and New Zealand, from the visa requirement for tourism trips of up to 30 days in 2026. Citizens of the countries on the e-visa list can apply online at evisa.mn.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules about goods you can take into or out of Mongolia and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty; if you become involved in a commercial dispute or a criminal investigation about a customs matter, you may be held in Mongolia until it is resolved.

The UK Foreign Office says you can take in up to 15 million Mongolian tugriks, and to declare cash or travellers' cheques worth 10,000 US dollars or more. Canada's travel advice says penalties for illegal drugs are severe, with jail sentences and heavy fines.

tips.text: The visa waivers for the countries on the Immigration Agency's 2026 tourism list (among them France, the UK, Australia and New Zealand) are temporary, and South Korea's standing waiver runs to 31 December 2026. The Embassy of Mongolia in London says the temporary 30-day tourist visa exemption is only valid until the end of 2026.
Mongolia's Immigration Agency says the individual or legal entity providing your housing must register you within 48 hours (Law on the Legal Status of Foreign Nationals, Article 24.4).
Canada's travel advice says U.S. dollars and credit cards are accepted in hotels and some restaurants, mainly in Ulaanbaatar, and advises carrying local currency, especially in rural areas.

The UK Foreign Office says weather conditions range from +35°C in summer to -40°C in winter and during the nights, that they often change without warning, and that there are frequent warnings for heavy snow and blizzards. It says only about 10% of roads outside the capital are tarmacked.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mongolia?
faq.answer: Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists standing visa waivers for, among others, the US, Kazakhstan and Brazil (up to 90 days), Germany, Canada, Japan and the UAE (up to 30 days), Hong Kong (up to 14 days) and South Korea (up to 90 days, until 31 December 2026, for tourism only). Its Immigration Agency says the Government has exempted nationals of 34 countries, among them France, Spain, Italy, the UK, Australia and New Zealand, for tourism trips of up to 30 days in 2026. Citizens of the countries on the e-visa list can apply online at evisa.mn.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in Mongolia visa-free?
faq.answer: Up to 30 days. Mongolia's Immigration Agency lists EU countries such as France, Spain and Italy among the 34 countries exempted from the visa requirement for tourism trips of up to 30 days in 2026; Germany has a standing waiver of up to 30 days on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list.

faq.question: How does the Mongolian eVisa work?
faq.answer: Mongolia's Immigration Agency says you go to evisa.mn, fill out the application form and pay the e-visa fee; if the application is approved, the Electronic Travel Authorization is sent to your e-mail within 48 hours. It says the K2 tourism e-visa is for up to 30 days.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Mongolia?
faq.answer: Mongolia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists US passport holders as able to visit without a visa for up to 90 days, under an arrangement in force since 6 July 2001. Under Article 24.4 of the Law on the Legal Status of Foreign Nationals, whoever provides your accommodation must register you within 48 hours.

faq.question: Do I have to register with immigration in Mongolia?
faq.answer: Yes. Mongolia's Immigration Agency says Article 24.4 of the Law on the Legal Status of Foreign Nationals requires individuals or legal entities providing housing for a foreign national to register them within 48 hours, online through the agency's website or its mobile application.
